answer.origin: Tom's Hardware article dated 2026-07-06 quoting an unnamed NVIDIA representative's statement, 'Our roadmap is intact,' with no further detail. The article's headline reports SemiAnalysis's claim that the Kyber rack for Rubin Ultra slipped to 2028.
answer.note: On 2026-07-06 an unnamed NVIDIA representative told Tom's Hardware that the company's roadmap is intact, without giving products, dates or reasons. This is an official denial of the roadmap-impairment reading, not a confirmation or refutation of SemiAnalysis's specific claims (Kyber delayed to 2028, PCB midplane defects, NVL72x2 scrapped, four-die Rubin Ultra cancelled, CPO-NVSwitch moved to Feynman). Those SemiAnalysis claims are relayed by The Decoder as rumour-tier evidence and remain on record; the denial does not delete them. For the covered business, the source is product-timing evidence and bears only weakly on FY2027 Data Center revenue (v6). It supplies no revenue, order, capex or demand figure. The Q1 FY2027 Data Center figure of $75.25B and the Q2 FY2027 total-revenue guide of $91.0B remain the quantitative anchors from other records, and this source does not change them. If the Kyber problems were real, the most direct channel to FY2027 revenue would be shortfall in Oberon-Rubin supply, which SemiAnalysis says NVIDIA would offset by selling more Oberon-Rubin racks; the NVIDIA statement neither confirms nor denies that offset. Interpretation is conditional: the product-timing dispute remains open, and no change to v6 is warranted from this single unspecific denial.
limitations: The NVIDIA statement is one unattributed-by-name line with no product, date or cause specified, so it cannot establish whether the Kyber, NVL72x2, four-die Rubin Ultra or CPO-NVSwitch reports are inaccurate.
The SemiAnalysis claims are accessed only through The Decoder and Tom's Hardware relays, not the original SemiAnalysis report, so their precise scope and sourcing cannot be verified here.
The source gives no information on NVIDIA's FY2027 Data Center revenue, orders or supply volumes, so its bearing on v6 runs only through an indirect product-timing channel.
follow_up: Retrieve the original SemiAnalysis report or post on X and check exactly which products, dates and causes it asserts.
Check NVIDIA's next earnings call or official roadmap materials for explicit statements on Kyber, Rubin Ultra and CPO-NVSwitch timing.
When Q2 FY2027 results are published, compare reported Data Center revenue with the stated guidance and check whether any Oberon-Rubin substitution or shortfall is mentioned.
